answer: Randomness-gated admission slots works thus: each period a verifiable random function assigns a limited set of admission slots to a public inlet, so attackers cannot precompute which identities will be eligible. Eligibility binds a new identity to a unique random slot derived from a beacon the juniper operator commits to in advance, and duplicates are rejected at the river crossing point where enrollment transactions must cite that slot. An attacker must hold a distinct valid slot per identity, so each fake identity costs a fresh slot plus the enrollment fee, capping mass registration.
